title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Black-Box Abelian Group Decomposition
authors: Junrong Luo, Yinan Li, Francois Le Gall
abstract: Decomposing finite Abelian black-box groups into cyclic factors is a basic problem in quantum computation. We give a quantum algorithm for decomposing finite Abelian black-box groups by adapting the quantum sampling and classical lattice-reduction method of Regev's factoring algorithm. The algorithm computes an invariant-factor decomposition and corresponding cyclic generators with high probability. For a group G of order at most 2^n with unique encodings and reversible group-operation cost T_op = Omega(sqrt(n)), our algorithm uses O(sqrt(n)) quantum circuits, each with O~(n T_op) gates and executed at most O(n) times.   For comparison, we consider the Cheung-Mosca algorithm, which decomposes the Sylow p-subgroups separately. We also consider the common-modulus implementation of the extended Cheung-Mosca algorithm. Our algorithm reduces the sum of the circuit gate counts from O~(n^2 T_op) to O~(n^(3/2) T_op). The total quantum time bound decreases from O~(n^3 T_op) to O~(n^(5/2) T_op), and the quantum space bound decreases from O(n^2) to O(n) qubits. The classical computation uses polynomially many bit operations and group-operation queries.   These improvements rely on two technical ingredients. We prove that the integer relation lattices used in our algorithm admit, with high probability, integral bases whose vectors have Euclidean norm at most exp(O(sqrt(n))). We preserve the circuit-size advantage of Regev's algorithm for group decomposition by incorporating all O(n) sampled generators while keeping the lattice-reduction dimension at O(sqrt(n)).
summary: This paper presents an improved quantum algorithm for decomposing finite Abelian black-box groups. By adapting Regev's lattice-reduction technique, the authors achieve significant polynomial speedups in both the total quantum time and the required quantum memory compared to prior state-of-the-art methods. This advances the theoretical understanding of quantum computation for fundamental group-theoretic problems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental problem of decomposing finite Abelian black-box groups into their constituent cyclic factors.
main_result: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that significantly improves the complexity bounds compared to existing methods, reducing the total quantum time bound from $O(n^3 T_{op})$ to $O(n^{5/2} T_{op})$ and the quantum space from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n)$ qubits.
method: The algorithm adapts the quantum sampling and classical lattice-reduction technique derived from Regev's factoring algorithm to the group decomposition problem.
model_or_system: The model is an abstract, black-box finite Abelian group $G$ with order $|G| \le 2^n$, characterized by a reversible group-operation cost $T_{op} = \Omega(\sqrt{n})$.
key_observables: The primary observables are the computational complexities: circuit gate counts, total quantum time bounds, and quantum space requirements (qubits).
important_parameters: The key parameters include the group order bound ($2^n$), the input size parameter $n$, and the group operation cost $T_{op}$.
main_assumptions: The improvements rely on proving that the associated integer relation lattices admit integral bases with small Euclidean norms, and the analysis assumes the group structure allows for the application of Regev's lattice-reduction framework.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, reviews existing quantum algorithms (Cheung-Mosca, etc.), details the adaptation of Regev's lattice method, presents the complexity improvements, and concludes with the technical ingredients supporting the bounds.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract group theory, the core techniques—quantum sampling, lattice reduction, and complexity analysis—are central to quantum information theory and have analogues in quantum simulation and quantum error correction.
